overallSummary: The repository provides a well-organized multi-layer agent context. Core routing is strong, and most key areas have dedicated documentation. Primary risks are context size, limited duplication, and a few coverage gaps in peripheral areas.
strengths: AGENTS.md provides a clear authority hierarchy and explicit routing to skills, docs, and configuration.
Skills are well-scoped, task-specific, and include verification steps.
Documentation is organized by purpose (architecture, content, deployment, testing, decisions, design system).

priorities.finding: Reduce duplicated guidance across AGENTS.md, README.md, and testing.md — command tables and notes appear in all three files with minor variations.
priorities.recommendation: Establish AGENTS.md as the sole source for agent-facing commands and threshold references. Replace tables in other files with links to AGENTS.md.

priorities.finding: Active context size is high (~41K estimated tokens) for the standard agent context path. The Figma agent brief alone is ~26KB and rarely relevant.
priorities.recommendation: Move the Figma brief out of the default agent context path into a task-specific reference. Consider splitting or summarizing other large docs.

priorities.finding: Finding: Contact-worker documentation lives in docs/deployment.md but is not independently discoverable from the context path.
priorities.recommendation: Add an explicit routing entry in AGENTS.md for contact-worker changes, or create a separate contact-worker docs file linked from deployment.md and AGENTS.md.

metrics.label: Context Precision
metrics.interpretation: Most context documents are relevant, but several files (figma brief, todo list, project overview) add marginal value for common tasks.

checks.label: Core routing files are directly relevant to agent tasks
checks.evidence: AGENTS.md, README.md, and all skills serve clear agent-task purposes.

checks.label: Documentation maps to specific change types without excessive scope
checks.evidence: AGENTS.md 'Before making significant changes' table routes each change type to the correct doc.

checks.label: Design-system files are relevant without unnecessary breadth
checks.evidence: docs/design-system/agent-guide.md and README.md are directly relevant. figma-agent-brief.md (26KB) is Figma-generation specific and adds context weight without proportional value.

checks.label: Context is free of off-topic or archived content
checks.evidence: docs/todo.md and docs/project-overview.md are low-signal files for the agent context path. todo.md contains an unchecked pre-launch checklist; project-overview.md largely duplicates README.md.

checks.label: Command tables do not inflate the relevant context
checks.evidence: Command tables in AGENTS.md, README.md, and testing.md repeat similar content across three files, adding ~500 bytes of duplicated text.

metrics.label: Context Recall
metrics.interpretation: Most context sources are reachable through AGENTS.md routing. A few areas lack direct routing.

checks.label: AGENTS.md routes to all major documentation areas
checks.evidence: The 'Before making significant changes' table and 'Skills' section cover architecture, content, styling, deployment, testing, content schema, and contact-worker areas.

checks.label: Skills cover the declared task types
checks.evidence: Nine skills (safe-change, astro-implementation, performance-budget, a11y, design-system-css, pagefind, seo-review, code-quality, copy-edit) match the listed categories.

checks.label: Design-system documentation is discoverable from the context path
checks.evidence: AGENTS.md routes to docs/architecture.md which lists design-system entry points. design-system/ directory has README.md, agent-guide.md, and inventory.json.

checks.label: Contact-worker guidance is independently discoverable
checks.evidence: Contact worker guidance is embedded in docs/deployment.md without a dedicated routing entry from AGENTS.md. An agent must already know to look in deployment docs.

checks.label: Specifications are reachable
checks.evidence: specs/ directory has a README.md explaining usage, but AGENTS.md does not reference specs/. Agents following only AGENTS.md may miss existing specifications.

metrics.label: Sufficiency
metrics.interpretation: Repository guidance covers most common tasks well. Gaps exist in peripheral areas.

checks.label: Architecture and routes are documented
checks.evidence: docs/architecture.md covers core areas, generated areas, integrations, and sources of truth.

checks.label: Content authoring has complete workflow documentation
checks.evidence: docs/content-authoring.md covers creating, drafting, previewing, publishing, unpublishing, and updating articles.

checks.label: Testing and validation commands are documented
checks.evidence: docs/testing.md, AGENTS.md commands table, and validation table all cover the available checks.

checks.label: Design-system documentation covers component inventory
checks.evidence: Inventory.json catalogs all reusable patterns. Agent-guide.md explains how to use it.

checks.label: Structured data and metadata are documented
checks.evidence: docs/structured-data.md covers schema location, report generation, and validation.

checks.label: Performance, SEO, and accessibility have documented quality standards
checks.evidence: docs/performance-seo-accessibility.md is brief (1243 bytes). The detailed guidance lives in skills (performance-budget, accessibility, seo-review). This split requires loading skills to get the complete picture.

checks.label: Contact-worker changes have a dedicated documented workflow
checks.evidence: Contact-worker changes are mentioned in change-policy.md and deployment.md but there is no dedicated contact-worker documentation entry in AGENTS.md.

metrics.label: Authority Clarity
metrics.interpretation: Most guidance has a clear canonical source, but several topics have duplicated instructions across files.

checks.label: Command definitions have a single authoritative source
checks.evidence: Commands appear in AGENTS.md, README.md, and docs/testing.md. While each serves a different audience, agents encounter all three and must reconcile minor variations.

checks.label: Discipline checklists are not duplicated across files
checks.evidence: Accessibility guidance appears in .agents/skills/accessibility/SKILL.md, docs/performance-seo-accessibility.md, and the design-system documentation. These are broadly consistent but use different language.

checks.label: Skills do not conflict with each other
checks.evidence: Each skill is scoped to a specific task type. Design-system-css and accessibility skills cover distinct concerns. No contradictory guidance found.

checks.label: Documentation decisions have recorded rationale
checks.evidence: docs/decisions/ contains four ADRs covering architecture, contact-worker separation, Pagefind search, and structured data.

checks.label: Environment configuration has a single authoritative file
checks.evidence: .env.example is the canonical template. No duplicated env documentation outside docs/deployment.md.

checks.label: Content schema has clear, non-duplicated documentation
checks.evidence: src/content.config.ts is authoritative. docs/content-model.md is a human-readable reference. No other schema documentation exists.

metrics.label: Active Context Size
metrics.interpretation: The default agent context path is approximately 163,381 characters (~40,845 estimated tokens at 4 chars/token). This is large for a personal blog repository.

details.estimationMethod: Approximately 4 characters per token for English prose. Not a real tokenizer.

methodology.scoring: Each agent-assessed metric uses weighted checks (pass=1.0, partial=0.5, fail=0.0). The metric score is the weighted average of its checks. Assessments are based on repository inspection by a coding agent and reflect the agent's judgment. They are not authoritative measurements of context quality for all tasks or agents.
methodology.tokenEstimation: Estimated tokens = total characters / 4. This approximates English prose tokenization (approximately 4 characters per token). It is not a real tokenizer and may vary significantly for code, markup, or non-English content.

limitations: Semantic checks (precision, recall, sufficiency, authority) are assessed by a coding agent and reflect its judgment. Different agents or humans may reach different conclusions.
Token estimation uses a fixed 4-characters-per-token approximation. Real tokenizer output may differ by 20-30%.
The active context path is defined as the set of files a standard agent session would typically load. Actual context paths vary by task and agent configuration.
The report does not measure LLM output quality, factual accuracy, security posture, or production runtime behavior.
Findings are based on a single audit pass and may not catch all issues.
